learning_outcomes.text: Understand and master the fundamental concepts of linear algebra and affine geometry.
Solve concrete problems using linear algebra tools.
Critically analyze results and solution choices.
Present mathematical language and content with rigor.
Acquire tools to continue the study of related disciplines.

Become familiar with the notions of vector space, linear function, matrices and their properties, scalar products, symmetric bilinear forms, and achieve a good command of calculation with vectors and matrices.
Be able to apply these results to the resolution of concrete problems in linear algebra and simple problems in analytic geometry concerning linear subvarieties of an affine space.

syllabus_topics: Algebraic structures: groups, rings, fields, real and complex numbers.
Linear applications: matrices, row reduction, invertibility, linear systems, determinants.
Vector spaces: subspaces, bases, dimension, coordinates, change of bases, sums.
Eigenvalues and eigenvectors, diagonalizability, similar matrices.
Scalar products: norm, angle, orthogonality, Gram-Schmidt, orthogonal matrices.
Symmetric bilinear forms, symmetric matrices, Spectral Theorem.
Affine geometry: affine spaces, points, lines, planes, incidence, distance.
Notes on algebraic structures such as groups, rings, and fields; the field of complex numbers.
Intersections, sums, and direct sums of vector subspaces.
Matrices associated with a linear function.
Reduction of a matrix to row echelon form.
Eigenvalues, eigenvectors, and eigenspaces of an endomorphism or a matrix.
Scalar products in real vector spaces.
Norm of a vector, angle between two vectors.
Orthogonality between vectors and between vector subspaces.
Real symmetric matrices and their diagonalizability.
Points, lines, and planes in space.
Linear subvarieties of an affine space.
teaching_methods: Lectures with tablet PC and projector support
Use of didactic technologies (Moodle, software, videos, quizzes, Wooclap)
Lecture notes in PDF format available on Moodle
Videos of lectures available on YouTube

assessment_methods.method: Written exam (theoretical questions and applied exercises)
Integrative oral exam (at the discretion of the lecturer)

assessment_rules: Learning verification occurs through a written exam consisting of theoretical questions and applied exercises. At the discretion of the lecturer, an integrative oral exam may also be requested. The use of generative artificial intelligence tools is not permitted. The criteria for evaluation are the completeness of acquired knowledge and the ability to apply knowledge to solve concrete problems.
